body:
This should be handled by the io.quarkus.security.runtime.interceptor.RolesAllowedInterceptor now. 

Do you have a reproducer?

I think you might have to declare the function as 'open'.

That said we really should throw a deployment error for this case.

Hi, 

thanks for info. I will check it. I have a small project [here](https://github.com/p-zalejko/my-planner/tree/v0.0.4). There is ```GreetingResourceTest``` and it fails when in pom.xml 0.27 is set.
@stuartwdouglas  thanks!, you are right, I changed these methods to ```open``` and now everything is fine.
@mkouba it looks like ArC is just ignoring final methods for interceptors, is this intentional? It seems like a big problem for cases like this.
Maybe if interceptors have been applied to final methods on application classes we could use our class transformers to make it 'just work' by removing the final modifier.
@stuartwdouglas That could be a general strategy for Kotlin, although it's probably better if we actually implement the kotlin compiler addon which would open things we deem necessary to be open.

Yes, we do ignore the final methods. The CDI spec requires a class that has a bound interceptor to be proxyable - no final methods. But we're a bit more lenient. I think we log a warning for each ignored final method...

> Maybe if interceptors have been applied to final methods on application classes we could use our class transformers to make it 'just work' by removing the final modifier.

Sounds interesting. But I wonder if there could be any "hidden" problems with this approach?
I think this behaviour is a big problem for security interceptors, especially if the interceptor has been bound to the method rather than the class
Isn’t it the Kotlin extension job to open the useful classes ?

This is not really a kotlin specific issue IMHO. If you apply a security annotation to a class it should either work, or cause a deployment error. Ignoring @RolesAllowed because a method is final is likely CVE material.

I completely agree with what @stuartwdouglas about failing on `final`.
On the other hand, making things non final is part of Kotlin support - not necessarily the extension but the Kotlin compiler addon we should to write (since our proposed changes to the generic all-open one got rejected)
Is someone working on the deployment error approach? I think we should have it in 0.28.0.
I am not, but I can get to it in a few hours if no one picks it up sooner.

It should be possible to throw a deployment error for non-proxyable types annotated with a security annotation. On the other hand, I'm not quite sure it should be the default behavior.  

Currently, we have a concept of "validation rules" that could be skipped: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/master/independent-projects/arc/processor/src/main/java/io/quarkus/arc/processor/BeanDeploymentValidator.java#L31-L33. We could use something similar for non-proxyable types.
